div.head: Tab 2
div.p: In connection with the Memorandum which was handed by State-Secretary Dukwits to Ambassador Tsarapkin on February 24, 1969, the Soviet side would like to state the following.

The Soviet side already gave on February 6 a comprehensive reply to the questions of interest to the West German side. As it was pointed out, the Soviet Union proceeds from the fact that as a party to the Treaty on nonproliferation of nuclear weapons the Federal Republic of Germany would together with the obligations taken on itself, enjoy in full measure the rights provided for in the Treaty equally to all non-nuclear states signatures to the Treaty. This naturally concerns all the provisions contained in the nonproliferation Treaty.

While working out the Treaty and the Security Council Resolution No. 255 no additional provisions were formulated concerning some individual states, the Federal Republic of Germany included, which would give them some special rights or, to the contrary, would place them in position of discrimination.
